subject.title: fix: Windows /restart falls back to in-process restart without changing PID

question: Should env-less native Windows gateways probe an installed Scheduled Task and use the supervised restart handoff, or should OpenClaw keep the current env-marker-only contract?
rationale: Current code intentionally avoids unsafe unmanaged detached respawn, but the reported setup has a Scheduled Task installed without inherited markers; deciding to add OS probing changes the restart fallback contract for existing Windows users.

options.title: Review and land the safe Scheduled Task probe
options.body: Accept the direction of the linked PR once it resolves exact task-name selection and provides real Windows restart proof.

options.title: Keep env-marker-only supervision
options.body: Require users to start through the Scheduled Task or reinstall/repair the service, and document the limitation instead of adding a runtime probe.

options.title: Design a broader Windows restart recovery path
options.body: Pause the narrow fix and handle env-missing detection together with broader Windows restart reliability issues such as failed `schtasks /Run` recovery.

recommendation.title: Review and land the safe Scheduled Task probe
recommendation.body: Accept the direction of the linked PR once it resolves exact task-name selection and provides real Windows restart proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This account introduced and merged the core Windows Scheduled Task restart path that defines the product contract at issue.
